network.description: Check IPv4, IPv6, NAT mapping behavior, and direct-connection readiness for hosting a server.
network.emptyDescription: Run a check to detect your public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, NAT mapping type, and practical advice for direct connections.
network.privacyNote: Only queries public STUN servers (stun.cloudflare.com, stun.miwifi.com, stun.l.google.com, stun1.l.google.com) when you start a check. Results stay on this PC.

natSummary.openInternet: Your PC holds a public IPv4 address directly with no address or port translation.
natSummary.endpointIndependent: Endpoint-independent mapping (Cone NAT): the same external port is reused across STUN servers.
natSummary.addressPortDependent: Address/port-dependent mapping (Symmetric NAT): each remote server sees a different external port.
natSummary.behindNat: Your IPv4 traffic is translated by NAT, and only one STUN server replied so Cone vs. Symmetric could not be distinguished.
natSummary.unreachable: No STUN server replied over IPv4 UDP.
natSummary.proxied: Traffic is leaving through a local proxy or VPN tunnel (TUN), so STUN may see the proxy's exit address or a mix of proxied and direct routes. The result cannot describe your real NAT type.

network.cgnatBadge: Carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10) detected on the local route.
network.directIpv6Label: IPv6 (recommended when both sides have IPv6)
network.directIpv4Label: IPv4 (requires Windows Firewall & router port forwarding if behind NAT)

advice.ipv6DirectReady: You have a global public IPv6 address. Friends with IPv6 can connect directly via [<ipv6>]:<port> once TCP is allowed in Windows Firewall and your router's IPv6 firewall.
advice.ipv6BehindNat: Your IPv6 traffic reaches the internet, but the public address differs from your local address (NAT6). Check your router's IPv6 forwarding or firewall rules.
advice.ipv6Unavailable: No public IPv6 route was detected. If your ISP supports IPv6, enabling it on your router often makes direct hosting easier than IPv4 NAT.
advice.ipv4OpenDirect: Your device has a direct public IPv4 address. Allow the Minecraft server TCP port in Windows Firewall so friends can join directly.
advice.ipv4ConeForward: Cone NAT detected on IPv4. Set up TCP port forwarding on your router if your router's WAN address is public (not CGNAT).
advice.ipv4SymmetricWarn: Symmetric NAT detected on IPv4. Direct IPv4 hosting and NAT traversal rarely work here; use IPv6 direct connect, a virtual LAN (such as Tailscale or ZeroTier), or a hosted server.
advice.ipv4BehindNatSingleProbe: IPv4 is behind NAT, and only one STUN server responded. Run the check again or test from another network to confirm whether NAT is Cone or Symmetric.
advice.ipv4CgnatDetected: Your local route is inside the CGNAT range (100.64.0.0/10). Router port forwarding on IPv4 will not reach the public internet; prefer IPv6 or a virtual LAN.
advice.ipv4Unavailable: IPv4 UDP probes did not get a reply. Check your internet connection or firewall UDP rules.
advice.ipv4TunnelDetected: A local proxy or VPN tunnel (TUN mode) appears to be handling this check's UDP traffic. Turn off TUN mode, or let UDP 3478 and 19302 bypass the proxy, then run the check again. No direct-connect IPv4 address is shown because it would point at the proxy, not your home network.
advice.ipv4MixedEgress: The STUN servers saw different public IPv4 addresses. Dual-WAN or load-balancing routers and some carrier NATs do this, and so does a proxy or VPN that routes only part of your traffic. If one is on, turn it off and run the check again.
advice.proxyDirectUdpNote: A custom HTTP proxy is enabled in launcher settings. This check probes direct UDP traffic without using the HTTP proxy.

server.notFound: The server no longer exists. Refresh the list.
server.snapshotChanged: The saved server list changed. No bookmark was modified. Review the refreshed list before trying again.
server.busy: Another server or download operation is still running.
server.addressInvalid: Enter a valid hostname or IP address with an optional port.
server.portInUse: Another managed server is already using this port.
server.processUnavailable: The server process is not running, so this action is unavailable.
server.importInstaller: This is an installer, not a server. Run it to install the server, then import the folder it creates.
server.importArgsFile: This server only has Unix arguments files (win_args.txt is missing), so it cannot be imported on Windows.
server.importArgsInvalid: The server's win_args.txt contains unsupported or unsafe Java arguments, so it cannot be imported or started.
server.importNoJar: This folder has no server JAR the launcher can run.
server.importProperties: The server's server.properties sets {{key}} to a value the launcher cannot manage. Change it there, then import again.
server.importNotJar: This file is not a valid JAR.
server.importOwnData: This is the launcher's own data folder or a folder inside it. Choose the server's own folder.
server.importLinks: The server folder contains links, junctions or special files, so it cannot be imported.
server.importTooLarge: This server is larger than the launcher can import: more than 100,000 files, 32 GiB or 64 folder levels, or a JAR over 2 GiB.
server.importChanged: Some of the server's files changed or could not be read while they were copied. If it is running, stop it, then import again.
server.importedJarMissing: The imported server's JAR is missing from its folder. Import the server again.
server.importedArgsMissing: The imported server's win_args.txt arguments file is missing from its folder. Import the server again.
server.importedRecordInvalid: This imported server's record is damaged. Import the server again.
server.importNeedsFolder: This JAR cannot start on its own: it needs the libraries and server files of the folder it was installed in. Import that folder instead.
server.importPropertiesText: The server's server.properties is not UTF-8 text, is over 1 MiB or cannot be read. Save it as UTF-8, then import again.
server.importJarName: The launcher cannot run a JAR with this name: it must end in .jar, must not start with @ or -, and must not be a name Windows reserves. Rename it, then import again.
